messages:
Viola (Customer): Hey team — our Private deployment (VPC peered via Direct Connect) in eu-west-1 lost connectivity ~10:05 UTC. API calls time out or return 502. No app changes on our side. Seeing TLS handshake failures in client logs. Can you help?

Aisha (Support): Sorry about that, escalating to network/SRE. Do you see anything in Redwood Console logs for that org/route? Any recent peering changes or config pushes on your side?

Viola (Customer): Console shows repeated connection errors starting 10:04 UTC. We did enable a new on-prem switch earlier but no firewall or route changes.

InfraBot: alert: bgp-peer-eu-west1 flapping (peer 203.0.113.45) — 3 withdraws detected in 5m.

Kenji (Network Eng): Looking at provider telemetry — BGP neighbor with customer ASN is flapping, multiple route withdraws. Can you pls run these from your edge and paste results: 
```
show ip bgp neighbors
show ip route 10.0.5.0/24
traceroute -n 10.0.5.12
```

Viola (Customer): Pasting outputs: 
```
# traceroute
traceroute to 10.0.5.12 (10.0.5.12), 30 hops max, 60 byte packets
 1  10.254.0.1  1.1 ms  1.0 ms  1.0 ms
 2  * * *
 3  * * *
```

Viola (Customer): BGP neighbor shows: Connect: 0 (established earlier), then STALE/Idle after withdrawals.

Priya (SRE): Traceroute blackholes after first hop — suggests routing not learning prefix via Direct Connect after withdrawal. TLS handshake failures could be side-effect of asymmetric path or MTU/fragmentation. Can you also tcpdump on the edge for port 443 to see handshake: 
```
sudo tcpdump -i eth0 host 10.0.5.12 and port 443 -w /tmp/tls.pcap
```

Marcus (Platform): Also check that your egress allowlist still includes Redwood Private control plane/public peering IPs and that no firewall rule was accidentally tightened. Missed egress can cause control-plane heartbeats to fail and trigger session teardown.

Kenji (Network Eng): Two likely causes from provider: 1) BGP session instability — provider is rate-limiting or flapping due to BFD timers, 2) Route-map / community filtering on customer/provider edge removing prefixes after switch change. Quick checks: confirm peer ASN and neighbor IPs, compare BGP uptime (show ip bgp summary), and gather provider-side logs.

Viola (Customer): We ran tcpdump — saw SYN then no SYN-ACK back from 10.0.5.12 during incidents. Also saw ICMP frag-needed sometimes.

Priya (SRE): ICMP frag-needed suggests MTU/DF issues. Direct Connect sometimes enforces a 1500 MTU on the link. TLS with larger records may get blackholed if DF set. Short-term mitigation: enable MSS clamping on your edge or lower MTU on the host. Example iptables for MSS clamp: 
```
iptables -t mangle -A FORWARD -p tcp --tcp-flags SYN,RST SYN -j TCPMSS --clamp-mss-to-pmtu
```

Kenji (Network Eng): Also saw BFD configured on that peer — if BFD flaps it can drop BGP quickly. Provider suggests increasing BFD timers or disabling BFD temporarily to stabilize. Changing to 300ms/3 misses -> 900ms hold helped in past.

Aisha (Support): From product side, confirm TLS certs — but since SYN never completes, likely lower network layer. Can you also confirm DNS resolution? Private endpoints use split-horizon DNS; ensure your resolver isn't returning old public IP.

Viola (Customer): DNS resolves to 10.0.5.12 (private) — confirmed.

Marcus (Platform): For repro steps for infra team: 1) Observe BGP neighbor state on provider, 2) capture tcpdump on customer edge and on Redwood ingress if possible, 3) check for ICMP frag-needed and MTU mismatch, 4) review firewall rules for egress allowlist to Redwood control plane and peering IPs, 5) check BFD timers and route-maps.

Kenji (Network Eng): We coordinated with provider — they found route-map on customer edge that matched the new switch and suppressed routes to 10.0.5.0/24 after flap. Provider temporarily removed the filter and bumped BFD hold-time.

DeployBot: deploy: route-map-change-rollback applied to provider-edge at 10:18 UTC.

Viola (Customer): After provider change, traffic resumed and API 200s returned around 10:19 UTC. TLS handshakes OK now.

Priya (SRE): Marking incident as mitigated. Follow-ups: schedule controlled maintenance to reapply correct route-map, test BFD timers under load, confirm MTU on entire path, and add explicit egress allowlist docs for customers.

Kenji (Network Eng): Temporary remediation we did: removed erroneous route-map filter, increased BFD hold timer, asked customer to enable MSS clamping as a defense, provider confirmed stable BGP for 15m.

Viola (Customer): Thanks — will schedule internal change window to avoid accidental route filters. Appreciate the quick response. :thumbsup:

Aisha (Support): Filing a support postmortem with root cause: customer-side route-map + BFD sensitivities causing BGP withdraw -> routing blackhole -> TLS handshake failures + ICMP fragmentation hints. Action items: docs update, template checks for new switch rollouts, and a KB article for MTU/MSS clamping.

Marcus (Platform): I'll create a follow-up ticket to add automated checks in Console for BGP flaps and a knowledge check for Private deployments: ensure peering IPs and control plane CIDRs are whitelisted.

InfraBot: incident #INC-2026-274 created for postmortem and follow-ups.
